plan.purpose: For the designer or deck owner who just ran a rough brief and now wants to look at the proposed visual directions side by side, judge each by its mockup and palette, and pick one to build the deck in.
plan.title: Design directions for your deck
plan.composition: One full-width column that reads like an editorial lookbook. It opens on a ResultHeader whose title is the deck's topic, read from the result. Right under it, a thin band of three Facts gives the brief's tone, goal and audience: the frame every direction answers to. The mockups come next and are the largest thing on the page: a Section holding a three-column Grid that repeats over the drawn mockups, each one a full-width 16:9 Picture, so the directions can be compared at a glance. Below them, a second Section lays out each theme's specification in a three-column Grid repeated over the themes, in the same order as the mockups above. Each theme sits in its own Card: its name, its palette as Swatches, then a short list of Details with the rationale behind it. The polished brief's free-text notes go last, folded away in a Collapsible, because the reader rarely needs them. The page is flat and quiet, with no nested boxes and only the swatches for colour, so the themes' own colours stand out.

brief:
# Result page: slide_designer.generate_design_proposals_from_rough_brief

Transform a design brief into multiple themes with visual mockups and HTML report

## Frame

This page is the result page of an app that is composed, then shows its result: what the person sees after one run. The host draws what surrounds it: the band with the team's logo and the app's name, then a bar restating the request with a way back to edit it and to run again. The host also owns the actions on the result, such as downloading or sharing it, and places them where the page's header puts them. There is no side panel, no app bar and no footer to build, and nothing restates the request.

The page is the result across the full width. It opens on its header, which names the result in a person's words, read from the result itself where it can be (the page's h1). Then the figure or the fact a person looks for first, then the body of the result in the shape it naturally has: a plan day by day, options side by side to compare, a record's details. Lay out what a person reads; leave out what only a machine would.

## State

The host loads the run's result under `/result` before the page renders. Read every value with `$state`; emit no `/state` patches. Paths:

- `/result` — structure slide_designer.DesignDirections: The visual directions proposed for a deck: the brief as polished, each theme, and a title slide drawn in each
  - `/result/brief` — structure slide_designer.SlideDesignBrief — `brief`: The brief, as polished
    - `/result/brief/topic` — text — `topic`: The main topic or subject of the presentation
    - `/result/brief/brand_guidelines` — text — `brand_guidelines`: The client's brand guidelines (colors, fonts, logo usage, etc.)
    - `/result/brief/tone` — choice of "formal" | "playful" | "innovative" | "trustworthy" | "artsy" — `tone`: The tone of the presentation
    - `/result/brief/existing_references` — text — `existing_references`: Existing templates or past decks to reference or avoid
    - `/result/brief/goal` — choice of "pitch investors" | "sell to clients" | "internal training" | "keynote" — `goal`: The goal of the presentation
    - `/result/brief/audience` — choice of "executives" | "technical team" | "general public" — `audience`: The target audience
  - `/result/themes` — list of structure slide_designer.Theme — `themes`: The themes, one per direction
    - each item is a structure slide_designer.Theme (Complete presentation theme with colors, typography, layout, and style), with these members (paths relative to one item, for DataTable columns or $item):
      - `name` — text — `name`: Theme name identifier
      - `colors` — structure slide_designer.ColorPalette — `colors`: Color palette for the theme
        - `colors/primary` — text — `primary`: Primary brand color (hex or name)
        - `colors/secondary` — text — `secondary`: Secondary color for accents
        - `colors/accent` — text — `accent`: Accent color for highlights
        - `colors/background` — text — `background`: Background color
        - `colors/text_primary` — text — `text_primary`: Primary text color
        - `colors/text_secondary` — text — `text_secondary`: Secondary text color for subtitles
      - `typography` — structure slide_designer.Typography — `typography`: Typography settings
        - `typography/font_family` — text — `font_family`: Primary font family name
        - `typography/heading_style` — text — `heading_style`: Style description for headings (e.g., bold, uppercase)
        - `typography/body_style` — text — `body_style`: Style description for body text
      - `layout` — structure slide_designer.LayoutSettings — `layout`: Layout configuration
        - `layout/aspect_ratio` — choice of "16:9" | "4:3" | "1:1" — `aspect_ratio`: Slide aspect ratio
        - `layout/margins` — text — `margins`: Margin style (e.g., narrow, standard, wide)
        - `layout/alignment` — text — `alignment`: Default content alignment (e.g., left, center, right)
      - `style` — structure slide_designer.StyleSettings — `style`: Visual style settings
        - `style/overall` — text — `overall`: Overall visual style (e.g., minimal, corporate, creative)
        - `style/icon_style` — text — `icon_style`: Style for icons (e.g., outline, filled, flat)
        - `style/graphic_style` — text — `graphic_style`: Style for graphics and illustrations
      - `exclusions` — text — `exclusions`: Elements to avoid in the design (e.g., no gradients, no stock photos)
  - `/result/visuals` — list of image (a file) — `visuals`: A title slide drawn in each theme, in the same order
    - each item is a image (a file) (An image)

## Delegated

None. `MthdsResult` remains available for any structure you choose not to lay out.

## One real run, as loaded

The state of one actual run, so you can judge magnitudes and lengths. Bind to the paths; do not copy these values into the spec.
